iliana: Noticing a confusing DX bug in the Python SDK async embeddings helper used by the embeddings+rerank sample app: single-input async responses sometimes get unwrapped to a flat vector and rerank crashes.

ryan: Can you paste a tiny repro + the error you see?

iliana: Minimal repro (async):

```py
res = await client.embeddings.create(model='embed-small', input='single sentence')
print(type(res.data), len(res.data))
print(repr(res.data[0]))
```

Expected: res.data -> [list(float)]. Actual: intermittently res.data == [0.1, 0.2, ...] and rerank._prepare_docs does `for doc in docs:` -> TypeError: cannot iterate float. Happens under concurrency ~20% locally.

julie: That matches a bug where the async response normalizer calls _maybe_unwrap_singletons. Sync path always returns list-of-items. Race with batching timing explains nondeterminism.

ryan: Plan: 1) normalize inputs at callsite (wrap singletons), 2) ensure outputs are always list-of-items (remove async unwrap), 3) update typing and sampleapp, 4) add unit + integration tests. Nonbreaking migration if we normalize at entry.

docs-bot: Created issue: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/599 "async embeddings: singleton unwrap causes rerank shape mismatch". Added labels: dx, api-parity.

ci-bot: Noted a flaky test on windows in current PR run; adding deterministic test to catch interleaved batch unwraps.

julie: I'll open the PR with tests + sampleapp fix + changelog note. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

iliana: Thanks all, attaching local flaky repro to the issue and leaving this thread here.
